date_note: SANA's page, published 26 November, reports the Danish government's announcement and gives no earlier day.

evidence.quote: Unauthorised third parties have accessed the CPR data of 11,000 people

exec: The Local reports a new breach of Denmark's civil registry gave unauthorised third parties access to the CPR data of 11,000 people.
geo_basis: country: SANA reports the Danish government announcement from Copenhagen; the civil registry is a national system
plain: The Local reports Denmark's civil registry was breached again: unauthorised parties accessed the CPR data of 11,000 people. It says the breach was stopped and police arrested an 18-year-old man.

sources.name: The Local Denmark: New CPR number data leak in Denmark hits 11,000 people
SANA Arabic: new breach of the Danish civil registry affects data of 11 thousand people

summary: The Local reports the ministry said unauthorised third parties accessed the CPR data of 11,000 people; the breach was detected on 23 November and stopped, it says, thanks to a new monitoring system introduced after the first incident. The Local says police arrested an 18-year-old man, who was remanded in custody. SANA reports the same new breach, two months after an earlier attack.
title: Denmark reports new civil registry breach exposing data of 11,000 people, The Local and SANA report

validation.note: The Local Denmark and SANA each report the new CPR breach; SANA gives 'about 11 thousand' (Arabic), The Local gives 11,000 quoting the ministry.

review.note: SANA's Arabic says 'نحو 11 ألف' (about 11 thousand); the build's qualifier check cannot see the Arabic 'نحو', so 'about' cannot be written in the title/summary without a build error. Record left as '11 thousand'; a human should decide.
